correctness_confidence.basis: Core algebraic laws (Thms 2.2, 2.3), 1D/D-dim cyclic Gauss-Seidel recurrences (Thms 3.1, 3.2), doubly-exponential gap bounds (Thms 4.1, 4.2), and the su(3) AKLT determinant obstruction (Prop 6.1) check out mathematically; minor proof gaps exist in Thm 2.1 (m -> infinity passage), Thm 3.2(b) (non-asymptotic uniqueness of Q*_c(d)), Prop 4.3 (omitted 2*beta_n/L-length auxiliary bounds), and unspecified floating-point error radii for initial ED/Kaufman inputs.

novelty.basis: Substantial sharpening within the existing purity-bootstrap paradigm: exact piecewise-algebraic simplex squaring law on (0,1], staggered D-dim cyclic Gauss-Seidel thresholds (12.73x in 1D, 8x asymptotic single-Q), unbounded doubly-exponential gap transfer to all intervening even hypercubes, and the su(3) determinant no-go theorem for AKLT bond-RP.

reproducibility.basis: Manuscript specifies deterministic experiment/verifier scripts, exact-Q .cert.json replay, and zero-dependency Lean 4 audit manifest (not externally executed in this PDF-only review), though exact error radii epsilon_j used to quantize floating-point ED/Kaufman outputs in Experiments 2-3 are not explicitly documented.

rigor.basis: Strong formal rigor for the 16 algebraic lemmas/theorems in Table 1 and the exact-Q replay logic (Thm 5.1), though Thm 2.1, Thm 3.1(b,c), Thm 3.2(a), Prop 4.3, Cor 4.4, Prop 6.1, and end-to-end floating-point error certification of base ED/Kaufman partition functions remain unverified by Lean or interval arithmetic.

significance.basis: Breaks the flat (log 2)/beta_0 ceiling and enlarges certifiable basins by an order of magnitude, enabling thermodynamic gap certification on non-integrable Spin-1 Heisenberg+D (L0=4) and Spin-1/2 dimerized Heisenberg (L0=6) chains where u<=0.01 fails; still constrained by correlation length xi (e.g., isotropic Spin-1 Heisenberg at L0=4 fails) and strict reflection positivity.

potential_errors: Theorem 2.1 proof (p. 4): Passing from finite-m minimizers on K_m(p) to Delta_+^infinity needs a short density/continuity argument.
Theorem 3.1(b) statement (p. 6): Needs explicit restriction p in (1/2, 1].
Theorem 3.2(b) proof (p. 7-8): Existence and uniqueness of fixed point for finite D >= 2 follows from convexity of -log h*(e^-u).
Proposition 6.1 (p. 14): Symmetric-part Ostrowski-Taussky note clarifies general U in U(3).
strengths: Exact extremal characterizations in Theorems 2.1-2.3 eliminate factor-of-2 losses at both spectrum squaring and gap extraction, with clean elementary algebraic proofs on (1/2, 1] and exact two-level attainment.

Staggered staircase state tracking (Eqs. 13-15) yields an exact telescoping hypercube identity Q^(n) and cyclic Gauss-Seidel updates, improving uniform thresholds by 12.73x in 1D and single-Q thresholds by 3.26x-7.63x (asymptotically 8x) in d=1..5.
Theorem 4.1, Theorem 4.2, and Proposition 4.3 break the flat (log 2)/beta_0 gap ceiling cleanly and transfer the asymptotic exponent without loss to all intervening even hypercube lengths.

Proposition 6.1 provides a crisp, decisive su(3) determinant obstruction showing det(M(U)) = -(2-c)^3 c^5 < 0 for all c in (0,2) and all U in U(3), explaining why AKLT fails bond-reflection positivity while c <= 0 succeeds.

Transparent scope reporting: honest diagnostics for isotropic Spin-1 Heisenberg at L0=4 < xi, explicit abstention at h=0.7 in ferromagnetic TFIM, and clear Table 1 mapping of which 16 algebraic theorems/lemmas are Lean-verified.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact closed-form piecewise-algebraic simplex squaring law h*(p) on all of (0,1] (Thm 2.1).
Staggered staircase hypercube invariant Q^(n) and 8x asymptotic single-Q threshold enlargement (Thms 3.1-3.2).
su(3) determinant obstruction proving Spin-1 AKLT violates bond-reflection positivity for all U in U(3) (Prop 6.1).
summary: The manuscript significantly sharpens the reflection-positive purity bootstrap of [14, 17, 7] by deriving (i) the exact piecewise-algebraic simplex squaring law h*(p) on (0,1], its three-line algebraic form h*_1(p) = 1 - (1-p)^2/(2p^2) on (1/2, 1], and the sharp spectral-gap ratio bound (Thms 2.1-2.3); (ii) the exact D-dimensional cyclic Gauss-Seidel recurrence yielding uniform thresholds p_c(d) (12.73x wider defect in 1D) and an asymptotic 8x single-Q improvement (Thms 3.1-3.2); (iii) an explicit doubly-exponential contraction bound breaking the (log 2)/beta_0 ceiling and transferring to all intervening even hypercubes (Thms 4.1-4.2, Prop 4.3) plus Kramers-Wannier dual certification for the g=2 ferromagnetic 1D TFIM (Cor 4.4); (iv) a 16-symbol zero-dependency Lean 4 algebraic kernel and an exact-Q replayable certificate architecture (Thm 5.1); and (v) an su(3) determinant obstruction proving that the Spin-1 AKLT chain (and all c in (0,2) bilinear-biquadratic chains) violates bond-reflection positivity for every U in U(3), contrasted with certified gaps on Spin-1 Heisenberg+D and Spin-1/2 dimerized Heisenberg chains (Prop 6.1, Sec 6). No unresolved material objections invalidate the main results, though several minor proof-completeness gaps and an overstatement regarding end-to-end 'zero-floating-point-trust' (given uncertified floating-point ED/Kaufman base evaluations) warrant minor revision.
weaknesses: End-to-end 'zero-floating-point-trust' framing in the Abstract and Section 5 is slightly overstated: while the replay verifier checks the bootstrap deduction and rational logarithm bounds strictly over Q, the initial finite-size purities p_hat_j in Experiments 2 and 3 are produced by standard IEEE-754 floating-point Kaufman/ED routines without a proved worst-case rounding/eigensolver error bound or reported epsilon_j.

Several major theorems are not included in the Lean 4 formalization (Table 1): Thm 2.1 (general k), Thm 3.1(b,c), Thm 3.2(a), the full D-dimensional cyclic GS induction in Thm 3.2(b)/Thm 4.1, Prop 4.3, Cor 4.4, Thm 5.1, and Prop 6.1 remain paper-only proofs.
Experiment 4 tests the 2D (D=3) certifier on synthetic reflection-positive hypercube defects rather than an actual 2D lattice quantum Hamiltonian.

In Section 6.3, the exact-Q certificates on Spin-1 Heisenberg+D (D >= 4.5) and Spin-1/2 dimerized Heisenberg (delta >= 0.35) operate in strongly gapped regimes; isotropic Spin-1 Heisenberg (D=0) remains out of reach at L0=4.
